newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO remains soft, ignoring crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO remains soft, ignoring crude gains.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were under pressure as cargoes remained unsold and ignored the gains seen on crude values, traders said on Wednesday.
NYMEX February crude prices rose by 14 cents and last traded at $25.25 per barrel.
January fuel oil swaps was last quoted at $113.50/$114.50, down from Tuesday's $114.50/$115, in line with soft physical fundamentals.

Traders said a South Korean cargo for lifting in February was offered at $1.50 per tonne premium to Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) South Korea basis. Most traders said the offer was too high.
A trader said there were still two cargoes for end-January lifting from South Korea that remained unplaced. Offers were under $1 premium to Singapore spot quotes.
Chinese stockpiling for the Lunar New Year was over. China is now looking at the second-half February market. "But they are not in a hurry to buy," said a local trader.
One of two Venezuelan cargoes belonging to a European trader was also unsold, traders said.
Physical prices for end-January lifting supplies were quoted at $116-$118 per tonne on Tuesday.
